comparator.route: Ordinary non-abroad Linguistics bachelor with first-listed supplementary linguistics minor packages in year two
comparator.sourceNotes: The prospective year pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of twelve required 5-EC linguistics and supporting methods/AI courses; zero-credit academic language and mentoring entries are excluded. Year two consists of six required 5-EC linguistics courses (30 EC) and two required 15-EC arts minors. The selected supplementary linguistics minor 1 uses the first three listed 5-EC courses (language developmental disorders, language and thought, social interaction); minor 2 lists exactly three 5-EC courses (speech/voice/hearing, Dutch as a second language and Python). The prospective page mistakenly labels each individual supplementary-minor heading 30 EC, whereas its prose requires two minors of 15 EC each and the adopted 2026–27 OER independently states a 30-EC total year-two minor. Treating the headings as additive would give 90 EC for year two, contradicting both sources and the programme total. The ordinary, non-abroad prospective year three includes 5 EC language proficiency, 10 EC professional development, 5 EC language norms, a 10-EC research thesis and 30 EC genuinely free space; the abroad variant is not combined. The 2026–27 OER names different year-three taught major units (Pragmatics and History of Dutch) from the indicative 2029–30 webpage (Language proficiency and Language norms). This is a difference between distinct academic years, not evidence that 2029–30 has a guaranteed adopted curriculum. The selected route follows the prospective year pages, and the formal OER is cited only for the second-year 30-EC minor-space total.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary non-abroad Linguistics bachelor with first-listed supplementary linguistics minor packages in year two
routeSelection.basis: The generic Linguistics bachelor has two prospective third-year routes; select the first listed ordinary non-abroad route. For the second-year 30 EC restricted minor choice, select the numbered supplementary linguistics minors and their first three 5-EC options in official order. This selects disciplinary depth without reference to UCR fit, while the 30-EC third-year free space remains open.

core: Language structure, diversity, acquisition, meaning and variation
Language processing, the brain, thought and human development
Artificial intelligence, computational linguistics and language technology
Speech, language disorders and language-related health
Multilingualism, language variation and language in social communities
Experimental, statistical, corpus and programming methods for language research
adjacent: Argumentation, communication, norms and second-language teaching
questions: How is human language acquired, structured, used and changed?
How do brain and cognition enable language and what happens when language is impaired?
How can computation and artificial intelligence analyse or generate human language?

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & communication
alternatives.concept: Investigate language through Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, perception, development, stylistics, rhetoric, media, sociology, experimental methods and data analysis. This is a related-fields response centred on language processing and communication; it does not provide a cumulative sequence in phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, sociolinguistics, corpus linguistics or speech-language pathology.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives substantial space to psycholinguistics, cognition, communication, social interaction and empirical methods while avoiding the claim that UCR offers a full Linguistics major.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology, rhetoric, stylistics, media and social-psychology foundations precede Psycholinguistics, perception, advanced cognition, persuasive communication, development and research synthesis. Formal prerequisites precede dependent courses; every course uses its exact planned term and seven are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Data, AI & language applications
alternatives.concept: Build programming, data management, statistics, machine learning, neural networks, algorithms and AI methods, then connect them to language through text data, text classification, large language models, psycholinguistics and stylistic analysis. Language is a specific application within a wider computing curriculum; UCR does not offer formal computational linguistics, corpus linguistics, speech recognition or language-technology engineering.
alternatives.labelReason: Nineteen computing, mathematics and data courses form the curriculum, while Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, higher cognition and stylistics provide the language connection. “Language applications” accurately limits the claim.
progression: Programming, data, mathematics, brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology and stylistics precede AI planning, machine learning, Psycholinguistics, deep learning, reinforcement learning, algorithms and advanced quantitative methods. All formal prerequisites precede dependent courses; exact planned terms pass and nine courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The closest programme studies human language processing, communication, media and social interaction. The second replaces fourteen communication, literature, media, sociology, psychology and philosophy courses with programming, databases, machine learning, AI, algorithms and mathematics. Each programme contains 105 EC absent from the other, well above the 30-EC floor.

candidates.label: Language and health
candidates.assessment: Psycholinguistics directly addresses aphasia, dyslexia and language impairment, and neuroscience and psychology provide relevant foundations. UCR nevertheless lacks the speech, voice, hearing, clinical language-disorder, assessment and intervention sequence needed for a coherent 24-course language-and-health curriculum. General biomedical and psychology courses would not repair that disciplinary gap.

selection.assessment: The language-cognition-communication programme is the strongest complete related-fields response to the target’s human-language core. A separately evidenced computational-linguistics and language-technology cluster supports a distinct data-and-AI programme, with language applications stated in proportion to the actual courses. Multilingualism and variation are addressed within the closest programme rather than relabelled as a third route. The remaining generator-backed language-and-health direction fails because one Psycholinguistics course and general neuroscience/psychology cannot supply speech, hearing, disorder, clinical assessment and intervention training. Production stops at two.

blocks: Both connect communication to biological systems; UCR Neurobiology does not teach speech, voice or hearing science.
Both directly study language acquisition, processing and experimental psycholinguistics; UCR gives less formal-linguistic depth.
Both study social interaction empirically; UCR Social Psychology does not teach conversation analysis.
Both develop argumentation and rhetorical analysis; UCR is not a linguistics-specific reasoning course.
Both examine how linguistic choices create meaning; UCR stylistics does not provide a full semantic-theory course.
Both teach Python programming; the comparator applies it specifically to language research.
Both work with collections of text data; UCR introduces text data within general data science rather than corpus linguistics.
Both address applied AI; UCR includes text classification and large language models within broader deep learning.
Both provide probability and inferential-statistics foundations; UCR is mathematical rather than language-data specific.
Both develop research design and statistical analysis for human-subject research.

notes.text: Radboud Linguistics provides a cumulative sequence in language structure, acquisition, phonetics, syntax, semantics, corpus and experimental linguistics, sociolinguistics, language disorders and a linguistics thesis. UCR can centre a programme on language, cognition and communication or combine computing with specific language applications. These are related-fields responses: UCR does not reproduce a full Linguistics curriculum, speech-language pathology or computational-linguistics sequence.
